metadata.title: State Independent Proof of Kochen-Specker Theorem with Thirty Rank-Two Projectors

nodes.name: Contextuality and measurement context
nodes.statement: A context is a maximal set of compatible (mutually commuting) observables; quantum mechanics is contextual when measurement results depend on which other compatible observables are measured simultaneously or previously.

nodes.name: Noncontextual hidden-variable (NCHV) theory
nodes.statement: A hidden-variable theory in which every observable carries a pre-determined value $v(\cdot)$ that is independent of the measurement context.

nodes.name: Mermin pentagram
nodes.statement: A diagram of ten three-qubit observables (the nine tensor products of single-qubit Paulis $\sigma_x^i,\sigma_z^i$ together with the triple products) arranged in five contexts of four mutually commuting operators each, with each operator appearing in exactly two contexts.

nodes.name: Rank-1 and rank-2 projectors (rays and planes)
nodes.statement: A rank-1 projector $P_i = R_i R_i^T$ in $\mathbb{R}^8$ is called a ray; a rank-2 projector $P_{i,j} = P_i + P_j$, the sum of two orthogonal rays, is called a plane.

nodes.name: Value function $v(\cdot)$
nodes.statement: An NCHV value assignment with $v(\cdot)=\pm 1$ for the Mermin observables, $v(\pm I)=\pm 1$, and $v(P_i)\in\{0,1\}$ for projectors.

nodes.name: Product rule
nodes.statement: For mutually commuting operators with $LM = N$, any NCHV value function satisfies $v(L)v(M) = v(N)$.

nodes.name: Sum rule
nodes.statement: For mutually commuting operators with $L+M = N$, any NCHV value function satisfies $v(L)+v(M) = v(N)$.

nodes.name: Mermin pentagram product relations
nodes.statement: The five context-product equations $v(\sigma_x^1)v(\sigma_x^2)v(\sigma_z^3)v(\sigma_x^1\sigma_x^2\sigma_z^3)=v(I)$, ..., $v(\sigma_z^1\sigma_z^2\sigma_z^3)v(\sigma_z^1\sigma_x^2\sigma_x^3)v(\sigma_x^1\sigma_z^2\sigma_x^3)v(\sigma_x^1\sigma_x^2\sigma_z^3)=v(-I)$.

nodes.name: Rank-1 completeness relations (40-ray, 15 contexts)
nodes.statement: Fifteen completeness relations $\sum P_i = I$ over the 40 Kernaghan-Peres rays, in which 20 projectors appear four times and 20 projectors appear twice each.

nodes.name: Rank-2 completeness relations (30 planes, 15 contexts)
nodes.statement: Fifteen completeness relations $\sum P_{i,j} = I$ obtained by pairing rays in (\ref{eq2}); 30 distinct rank-2 projectors each occur exactly twice.

nodes.name: Kochen-Specker theorem
nodes.statement: The predictions of quantum mechanics are incompatible with any noncontextual hidden-variable theory; in particular no NCHV theory can reproduce QM for systems of dimension $\geq 3$.
assumptions: NCHV theory assigns a context-independent value $v(\cdot)$ to every observable
conclusions: No consistent NCHV value assignment exists for the relevant set of observables

nodes.name: Mermin's ten-operator KS proof (three-qubit)
nodes.statement: The ten three-qubit observables of the Mermin pentagram admit no NCHV value assignment: the product rule applied to the five contexts forces $\prod = +1$ on the left and $-1$ on the right.
conclusions: No consistent assignment $v(\cdot)=\pm 1$ exists for the ten Mermin operators

nodes.name: Kernaghan-Peres 36-ray KS proof
nodes.statement: There exist 36 of the 40 Kernaghan-Peres rays in $\mathbb{R}^8$ that yield a state-independent proof of the KS theorem in the three-qubit system.
conclusions: No NCHV assignment is consistent with the chosen 36-ray completeness structure

nodes.name: Waegell-Aravind 40-ray KS proof
nodes.statement: Using all 40 Kernaghan-Peres rays in 15 completeness relations, the parity contradiction (even sum on the left vs.\ odd sum 15 on the right) gives a state-independent KS proof in $\mathbb{R}^8$.
conclusions: No NCHV assignment is consistent with the 40-ray structure

nodes.name: State-independent KS proof with 30 rank-2 projectors
nodes.statement: There is a state-independent proof of the Kochen-Specker theorem for the three-qubit system using only 30 rank-2 projectors arranged in 15 completeness relations of four planes each (\ref{eq4}); this is the smallest projector count for the eight-dimensional system associated with the Mermin pentagram.
conclusions: No NCHV value assignment satisfies all 15 relations of (\ref{eq4})
Hence NCHV theories are refuted using only 30 projectors

nodes.name: Multiplicity of 243 rank-2 proofs from (\ref{eq2})
nodes.statement: Because each rank-1 projector in a context can be paired with several partners to form a rank-2 projector, the rank-2 completeness structure (\ref{eq4}) is not unique; 243 such proofs can be constructed from (\ref{eq2}).
conclusions: There exist 243 distinct rank-2 KS proofs derived from (\ref{eq2})

nodes.name: Proof of TP412.5 (parity contradiction for rank-2 projectors)
nodes.statement: Each of the 30 rank-2 projectors appears exactly twice in the 15 completeness relations (\ref{eq4}); summing $v(P_{i,j})\in\{0,1\}$ on the left of (\ref{eq5}) yields an even number, while the right side equals $\sum 15\cdot v(I)=15$, an odd number, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Construct rank-2 completeness from rank-1
nodes.statement: Pair the rays in each rank-1 completeness relation of (\ref{eq2}) into rank-2 projectors $P_{i,j}=P_i+P_j$, obtaining 15 relations $\sum P_{i,j}=I$ in (\ref{eq4}).

nodes.name: Apply the sum rule
nodes.statement: Invoke the NCHV sum rule $v(L)+v(M)=v(N)$ for commuting $L+M=N$ to convert each operator equation in (\ref{eq4}) into a value-function equation (\ref{eq5}): $\sum v(P_{i,j}) = v(I)$.

nodes.name: Count occurrences (left-hand parity)
nodes.statement: Each of the 30 rank-2 projectors occurs exactly twice across (\ref{eq4}), so $\sum_{\text{relations}}\sum_i v(P_{i,j}) = 2\sum_{(i,j)} v(P_{i,j})$ is even.

nodes.name: Count right-hand side (odd total)
nodes.statement: The right-hand sides give $\sum_{k=1}^{15} v(I) = 15$, an odd number.

nodes.name: Derive parity contradiction
nodes.statement: An even number cannot equal 15, so no NCHV value assignment is consistent with (\ref{eq4}); the KS theorem is established with only 30 rank-2 projectors.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of TP412.2 (Mermin pentagram product contradiction)
nodes.statement: Apply the product rule to each of the five contexts of the Mermin pentagram (\ref{eq1}); every left-hand $v(\cdot)$ appears in exactly two equations, so the product over all five equations is $+1$ on the left, but the right yields $v(I)^4 v(-I)=-1$, a contradiction.

nodes.name: Write the five context product equations
nodes.statement: List the five context relations of (\ref{eq1}); the four `vertical' contexts give $+v(I)$ and the horizontal triple-product context gives $v(-I)$.

nodes.name: Multiply all five equations
nodes.statement: Each $v(\cdot)\in\{\pm 1\}$ on the left appears in exactly two contexts, hence the global left-hand product equals $+1$.

nodes.name: Right-hand global product
nodes.statement: The right-hand product equals $v(I)^4\cdot v(-I) = -1$.

nodes.name: Conclude contradiction
nodes.statement: Since $+1\neq -1$, no NCHV value assignment exists for the ten Mermin operators.

nodes.name: Proof sketch of TP412.4 (40-ray parity argument)
nodes.statement: Apply the sum rule to the 15 completeness relations (\ref{eq2}); since the 40 projectors appear with multiplicities 4 (twenty of them) and 2 (the remaining twenty), the left sum is even, while the right is $\sum_{k=1}^{15} v(I)=15$, odd: contradiction.

nodes.name: Hypergraph of orthogonality among the 30 planes
nodes.statement: The orthogonality relationships of the 30 rank-2 projectors of (\ref{eq4}) are depicted as a hypergraph (Figure 2) on 30 vertices, with the relabeling 1--20 for the first 20 entries of (\ref{eq4}) and 21--30 for $P_{1,2}, P_{3,5}, P_{9,13}, P_{14,15}, P_{19,21}, P_{28,30}, P_{23,24}, P_{31,32}, P_{34,36}, P_{33,38}$.

nodes.name: Cabello-style testable inequality
nodes.statement: The 30-projector proof can be cast as a noncontextuality inequality of the Cabello type that is violated by quantum mechanics for any state and satisfied by every NCHV theory.

nodes.name: Minimality claim for the eight-dimensional Mermin-pentagram setting
nodes.statement: Among state-independent KS proofs associated with the Mermin pentagram in $\mathbb{R}^8$, the present construction uses the smallest number of projectors known (30), beating the rank-1 records of 36, 38, and 40 projectors.

nodes.name: Kernaghan-Peres 40 rays in $\mathbb{R}^8$
nodes.statement: Five orthogonal octads $R_1$--$R_8$, $R_9$--$R_{16}$, $R_{17}$--$R_{24}$, $R_{25}$--$R_{32}$, $R_{33}$--$R_{40}$ in $\mathbb{R}^8$, with entries from $\{0,\pm 1\}$, generated from the Mermin pentagram operators (Table 1).

nodes.name: Minimum-projector state-independent KS proof
nodes.statement: Find a state-independent proof of the Kochen-Specker theorem in the three-qubit (eight-dimensional) system that uses the smallest possible number of projectors.
